messages:
sara-support: Heads-up — a dedicated customer hit consistent parse failures when using JSON_MODE + batching. They say some responses contain fields that belong to previous items (looks like objects got merged). Posting the snippet they sent and a short repro they ran.

sara-support: snippet from their logs (they pasted exactly):
```
EXPECT: [{
  "id": "a",
  "score": 0.98
}, {
  "id": "b",
  "score": 0.77
}]
GOT: [{
  "id": "a",
  "score": 0.98,
  "notes": "something"
}, {
  "id": "b",
  "score": 0.77,
  "notes": "something"
}]
```

sara-support: repro they posted (curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -H 'X-Redwood-Mode: JSON_MODE' 
  -d '{"inputs":["prompt for a","prompt for b"], "batching":true}'
```

mike-eng: thanks. couple quick q's — are they using any response_cache headers or a custom cache key? this sounds like cache entries getting mixed while assembling batched responses (race).

sara-support: they said they're on Dedicated, default cache settings. no custom cache key. they tried turning off caching on their end (set cache-control: no-cache at app layer) and issue went away for a few hours, came back later.

jess-ml: this pattern matches a race we saw once: when a batch contains both cache-hit fragments and live-generated fragments, the assembler could reuse a buffer and not clear metadata between items. there was a small refactor in the response-assembler fast-path last month (commit 8f3a2). could be that.

alex-sre: was there a deploy around the time the customer first saw it? deploy-bot, any canary notes? :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployed service/response-assembler v2.14 to canary at 2024-03-02T03:12:40Z (rollout=20%)

mike-eng: okay, if disabling cache at client side made it stop temporarily that strongly suggests cache-apply ordering bug. can we get a sanitized core dump or raw server responses? also pls try reproducing with batch size=2 and with cache disabled vs enabled. i'll prepare a small guard we can patch (clear per-item buffers + mutex around cache-apply in assembler).

sara-support: customer ran 3 quick tests:
1) cache on, batch=2 -> fail (~1/10 requests)
2) cache off, batch=2 -> pass
3) cache on, batch=1 -> pass
so it only happens when batching >1 and cache is active.

jess-ml: sounds deterministic enough to reproduce. i'll take a look at the assembler code path that merges cached fragments. quick repro script idea (pseudo):
```py
# fire two prompts concurrently with JSON_MODE and shared cache TTL
for _ in range(200):
  spawn(req([prompt_a, prompt_b], json_mode=True))
```
we should see ~1-5% malformed merges if it's the same bug.

alex-sre: i'm going to schedule a rollback of the v2.14 canary if we can confirm correlation. sara, can you collect the exact UTC when customer first saw error? we'll need to cross-check logs.

sara-support: they reported first seen 2024-03-02T04:05:12Z and started consistently around 04:07Z. i've attached sanitized request ids in the ticket (IDs: r-7a9, r-7b2).

mike-eng: good. i'll push a minimal patch to staging that adds: clear_item_buffer(item_idx) + metrics (malformed_json_count) and run our stress repro. if that reduces failures we'll push hotfix to canary and then prod.

jess-ml: also adding a parser-level fallback: if structured output parse fails, log the raw token stream and return structured error instead of best-effort merging. helps prevent customer apps from getting mixed objects silently.

alex-sre: agreed. i'll coordinate rollback windows and a canary rollout plan. tagging eng-runtime for a bug: ENG-RTC-4521.

mike-eng: assigning to @mike-eng and @jess-ml. sara, please reply to the customer with a workaround: set batching=1 or disable server-side caching for now. i'll update once staging runs finish. :thumbsup:

sara-support: will do. thanks team — i'll keep this thread updated when customer confirms workaround or when we have a hotfix timeline.
